entries.title: Boxed Mac and Canned Chili Dinner

before.title: Boxed Mac and Canned Chili Dinner
before.description: An easy chili mac using a whole box and a can. Make dinner and save a portion for another day.
ingredients_list: 1 box original macaroni and cheese, 7.25 oz
1 can beef chili with beans, 15 oz
shopping_list: 1 box original macaroni and cheese, 7.25 oz
1 can beef chili with beans, 15 oz
recipe_steps: Boil the macaroni in a saucepan following its box directions, usually 7-8 minutes after the water boils. Drain carefully.
Return the pasta to the pan. Mix in the cheese packet, butter and milk. The amounts listed suit a standard original box; follow your package if it differs.
Stir in the canned chili. Heat gently, stirring often, until hot throughout, about 3-5 minutes. Refrigerate spare portions promptly and reheat leftovers to 165°F.

entries.title: Boxed Beef Pasta with Green Beans

before.title: Boxed Beef Pasta with Green Beans
before.description: A familiar Hamburger Helper dinner with frozen green beans. Makes four meal portions; check your box's liquid amounts before starting.
ingredients_list: 1 box Hamburger Helper beef pasta, regular size
shopping_list: 1 box Hamburger Helper beef pasta, regular size
recipe_steps: In a deep skillet over medium-high heat, crumble and cook the beef for about 7 minutes, until it reaches 160°F. Spoon excess fat into a heatproof container.
Add the pasta and seasoning from the box, green beans, milk and water. If your box specifies different liquid amounts, use those. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low, stirring occasionally, until the pasta and beans are tender, about 10-12 minutes or the package time. Add a splash of water if needed. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes.

before.title: Chicken and Potato Enchilada Skillet
before.description: About 15 minutes of hands-on work and 55 minutes total. Small potato cubes simmer with canned chicken in a mild enchilada sauce.
ingredients_list: 1 lb russet potatoes, scrubbed and cut into small cubes
1 cup frozen diced peppers and onions
1 can cooked chicken breast, 12.5 oz, drained
1 can mild red enchilada sauce, 10 oz
shopping_list: 1 lb russet potatoes, scrubbed and cut into small cubes
1 cup frozen diced peppers and onions
1 can cooked chicken breast, 12.5 oz, drained
1 can mild red enchilada sauce, 10 oz
recipe_steps: Put the potatoes, frozen vegetables, drained chicken, enchilada sauce, water and taco seasoning in a deep skillet. Stir and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover and lower the heat. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are fork-tender and the chicken is hot throughout. Add a splash of water if the sauce begins sticking.
Sprinkle with cheddar, cover for a minute to melt, and serve. If the potatoes are still firm, keep simmering; their size changes the cooking time.

before.title: Four-Ingredient Ravioli Bake
before.description: About 15 minutes of hands-on work and 45 minutes total. Frozen cheese ravioli and jarred sauce make a simple pasta dinner.
ingredients_list: 1 bag frozen cheese ravioli pasta, 25 oz
shopping_list: 1 bag frozen cheese ravioli pasta, 25 oz
recipe_steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and oil a 9-by-13-inch baking dish. Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Boil the ravioli following the bag directions, then drain. Spread a little sauce in the dish. Add the ravioli and remaining sauce, then cover with mozzarella.
Cover with foil and bake for about 20 minutes, until bubbling and 165°F in the center. Uncover for 5 minutes to melt any remaining cheese; rest 5 minutes before serving.

before.description: About 15 minutes of hands-on work and 60 minutes total. Cooked chicken, boxed stuffing and zucchini make a filling oven dinner.
ingredients_list: 1 can condensed cream of chicken soup, 10.5 oz
shopping_list: 1 can condensed cream of chicken soup, 10.5 oz

before.title: Shortcut Biscuits and Sausage Gravy
before.description: Breakfast for dinner with store-bought biscuits and simple skillet gravy. Use biscuits that bake in about 15 minutes.
recipe_steps: Preheat the oven and bake the biscuits on a tray according to their package directions.
While they bake, crumble the sausage into a skillet over medium heat. Cook until it reaches 160°F, about 6-8 minutes. Stir in butter and flour; cook while stirring for 2 minutes.
Gradually stir in milk, breaking up any flour lumps. Simmer gently, stirring, until thickened, about 5 minutes. Add pepper and spoon the gravy over the baked biscuits.

entries.title: Mild White Bean and Spinach Quesadillas

before.title: Mild White Bean and Spinach Quesadillas
before.description: Creamy bean-filled tortillas with mild cheese and no raw meat to handle.
ingredients_list: 1/2 can cannellini beans, 15 oz can, drained and rinsed
shopping_list: 1/2 can cannellini beans, 15 oz can, drained and rinsed
recipe_steps: Mash the drained beans lightly in a bowl. Mix with the chopped spinach, cheese, sour cream and spices.
Spread the filling over half of each tortilla, then fold the empty half over it.

Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook the folded tortillas in batches for 3 to 5 minutes per side, until crisp and the filling is hot with melted cheese. Lower the heat if they brown too quickly.
Rest briefly, then cut into wedges. Refrigerate the unused canned beans in a covered container.
